question: A pregnant woman with moderate plaque psoriasis needs phototherapy. Which modality is preferred, and why?

answers.text: PUVA (psoralen + UVA), because it is the most effective phototherapy for psoriasis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. PUVA uses the photosensitiser psoralen, which is teratogenic and therefore contraindicated in pregnancy. Despite its efficacy, it is not the appropriate choice for pregnant patients.

answers.text: Narrowband UVB (311 nm), because it is effective and safe during pregnancy — unlike PUVA, it requires no photosensitiser

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Narrowband UVB at 311 nm is the preferred phototherapy for moderate psoriasis and is safe in pregnancy because it does not require a photosensitiser. PUVA is contraindicated in pregnancy because psoralen is teratogenic.

answers.text: Broadband UVB, because it carries no risk of phototoxicity whatsoever

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While broadband UVB avoids psoralen, narrowband UVB at 311 nm is more effective and has largely replaced broadband UVB in modern clinical practice.

answers.text: No phototherapy is safe in pregnancy; only emollients should be used

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Narrowband UVB phototherapy is well established as safe during pregnancy and is a standard treatment option for pregnant women with moderate psoriasis who need more than topicals.

overallFeedback.feedback: Narrowband UVB (311 nm) is the preferred phototherapy for psoriasis in pregnancy because it requires no photosensitiser. PUVA is contraindicated because psoralen is teratogenic.
Correct. Narrowband UVB is the phototherapy of choice in pregnancy — effective, psoralen-free, and safe for both mother and fetus.
